scope: HMAC secret rotation surface; audit_logs payload injection vectors; fiscal_alloc_error_at retry path attack surface; pilot-restrict / refund route authz; cash drawer manager-gate; gateway-context guard; Sanctum kiosk:order token surface vs fiscal allocation
method: Read of AuditLogService.php (secret resolution + assertProductionSafe), ZReportService.php (assertProductionSafe duplicate), FiscalSealingService.php, config/fiscal.php (dev_sentinels + min_secret_length), RetryFiscalAllocCommand.php, PaymentService.php (assertGatewayContext + assertPilotPaymentMethodAllowed), PosController.php (permission:pos middleware), Cash/CashDrawerService.php (variance gate + manager_gate_routine_close)
summary_findings: Security posture on POS x Fiscal is hardened and defense-in-depth across three layers: (1) production-safe secret enforcement (dev_sentinels blocklist + min 32-char length, refused at first signing attempt on APP_ENV=production, identical assertProductionSafe in both AuditLogService and FiscalSealingService — slight duplication acceptable), (2) per-branch HMAC secret override via FISCAL_AUDIT_SECRET_BRANCH_N for tenant rotation without affecting other branches' chains, (3) PaymentService::payment() guard requires gateway-callback context via backtrace walk (P0-POS-02) so queue workers / consoles / future controllers cannot forge PAID. Pilot-restrict (config payment.pilot_restrict) audit-logs every blocked attempt for forensics. Cash drawer adds variance gate (|variance|>threshold requires variance_reason + cash.reconcile.variance.override permission) and optional manager-gate on routine close. RetryFiscalAllocCommand only writes orders flagged with fiscal_alloc_error_at — it cannot allocate sequences for arbitrary orders. The audit_logs canonicalisation pipeline (sortRecursive + JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES|JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE) is deterministic across PHP versions and DB drivers, preventing payload injection via key-order-dependent hashing. No P0 / P1 emerged. Two P2 nits worth tracking for V1.0.X: env() reads inside AuditLogService::secretFor occur on every write (no config-cache miss but env() bypasses Laravel config cache — a 6-figure-row branch could trigger several thousand env() reads/sec under burst, no security risk but observability noise), and the dev_sentinels list is short (7 entries) and could grow as projects copy-paste from .env.example variants.

ROADMAP_P2.title: env('FISCAL_AUDIT_SECRET_BRANCH_'.$id) bypasses Laravel config cache
ROADMAP_P2.evidence: Line 273 `env('FISCAL_AUDIT_SECRET_BRANCH_'.$branchId)` is called inside secretFor() which is called on every write(). env() does NOT read from config:cache once cached. After `php artisan config:cache` in production, env() returns null for keys not loaded at boot, so the per-branch override silently degrades to the shared secret. This is actually the SAFE failure mode (chain stays consistent) but operators may set the env var expecting it to take effect on the next request without a config rebuild. Document in docs/FISCAL_SECRETS.md.
ROADMAP_P2.risk: Low — silent fallback to shared secret, not a chain break.
ROADMAP_P2.regression_cost: Zero (doc only). Code change would mean moving per-branch override into config/fiscal.php at boot, which is straightforward but out of scope V1.

ROADMAP_P2.title: dev_sentinels blocklist is finite (7 entries); not regex-based
ROADMAP_P2.evidence: Only literal strings are refused. A near-default like 'changeme!' or 'secret-key' would pass. The min_secret_length=32 catches short strings but a 32-char low-entropy string (`aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa`) would not. This is acceptable for V1 (the goal is to catch the most obvious .env.example mistakes), but a future P2 could add an entropy heuristic (Shannon entropy >= 3.5 bits/char) to reject low-entropy production secrets.
ROADMAP_P2.risk: Low — gross operator error catch only; sophisticated misuse requires explicit choice.

KEEP_AS_IS.title: AuditLogService::assertProductionSafe production-only refusal
KEEP_AS_IS.evidence: Refuses to sign if APP_ENV=production AND (secret in dev_sentinels OR strlen<32). Outside production, dev strings are allowed (CI stays fast). Throws RuntimeException with pointer to docs/FISCAL_SECRETS.md rotation runbook.
KEEP_AS_IS.verdict: Production-grade. The local-dev allowance is intentional and tested.

KEEP_AS_IS.title: FiscalSealingService duplicate assertProductionSafe
KEEP_AS_IS.evidence: Same logic as AuditLogService — slight duplication but the sealing service operates on a DIFFERENT secret (fiscal.z_report_secret vs fiscal.audit_secret) so factoring would couple two independent rotation surfaces. Acceptable as-is.
KEEP_AS_IS.verdict: Production-grade. Duplication is the right call for separation of secrets.

KEEP_AS_IS.title: PaymentService::assertGatewayContext backtrace-walk guard
KEEP_AS_IS.evidence: Walks debug_backtrace up to 25 frames searching for a subclass of \App\Services\PaymentAbstract. Throws HttpException 403 with Log::warning otherwise. Test/console opt-in via runtime container binding `payment.service.allow_direct_call`=true which is consumed (forgetInstance) on first read — single-shot, no leak. Non-spoofable from outside the gateway hierarchy.
KEEP_AS_IS.verdict: Production-grade. The P0-POS-02 guard is the right shape for V1 — defense-in-depth on a fiscally-significant action.

KEEP_AS_IS.title: Payload canonicalisation (sortRecursive + JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES)
KEEP_AS_IS.evidence: sortRecursive ksorts associative arrays at every depth, preserves list order (array_is_list short-circuit). json_encode with JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES|JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE removes the two most common cross-PHP/cross-driver hash drift sources. Throws RuntimeException on encoding failure (e.g. invalid UTF-8 payload) instead of silently writing a bad row.
KEEP_AS_IS.verdict: Production-grade. The canonicalisation is bit-stable across PHP 8.0+, MySQL, and SQLite.

KEEP_AS_IS.title: RetryFiscalAllocCommand scope-limited writer
KEEP_AS_IS.evidence: Only writes orders WHERE fiscal_alloc_error_at IS NOT NULL AND fiscal_sequence_no IS NULL — these are exactly the rows that the kiosk auto-allocate path failed on (iter14 SPECIALIST-3 marker). The command cannot allocate for arbitrary orders. Allocator is the same FiscalSequenceService::next, so all concurrency invariants apply.
KEEP_AS_IS.verdict: Production-grade. Surface is minimal and the retry path can only catch up legitimate orphans.

KEEP_AS_IS.title: Pilot-restrict audit log on rejected payment method
KEEP_AS_IS.evidence: isPilotPaymentMethodAllowed checks config('payment.pilot_restrict.allowed_methods', ['credit']). Block flow writes an audit_logs row with action='payment.method_restricted' (configurable) carrying the blocked_method, allowed_methods, actor identity, and order-vs-actor branch_id. Even if the audit write itself fails (try/catch around AuditLogService), the rejection still propagates as ValidationException — fail-closed.
KEEP_AS_IS.verdict: Production-grade. Forensic trail for restricted-pilot enforcement.

KEEP_AS_IS.title: CashDrawerService variance gate + optional manager-gate routine-close
KEEP_AS_IS.evidence: |variance|>threshold throws CashVarianceRequiresApprovalException 422 (custom error_code CODE_REASON_REQUIRED) when variance_reason is null/empty. cash.reconcile.variance.override permission required when approval_required=true (default true). Optional Sprint H2 F-11 manager-gate on routine close (any close, not just variance) reuses actorCanOverrideVariance — no duplicate permission path. Default off (single-cashier deploys), opt-in via CASH_MANAGER_GATE_ROUTINE_CLOSE=true.
KEEP_AS_IS.verdict: Production-grade. The variance gate is the canonical NF525 cash-shortage forensics pattern; the manager-gate routine-close is a SaaS-ready extension.

KEEP_AS_IS.title: Idempotent finally-release on Cache::lock (no double-release crash)
KEEP_AS_IS.evidence: Every Cache::lock acquisition is wrapped in try/finally with `try { $lock->release(); } catch (\Throwable $e) {}` so a double-release or expired-lock crash never masks the original exception. Best-effort by design.

adversarial_questions_considered: Q: Could a malicious branch admin rotate FISCAL_AUDIT_SECRET_BRANCH_X to a low-entropy value to forge audit rows? A: No on APP_ENV=production — assertProductionSafe rejects sentinels and short secrets. Outside production (dev/test) yes, but local dev does not have legal force.

Q: Could a payload field containing newline + JSON injection forge a different hash input? A: No. json_encode with JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES|JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE escapes control characters and quotes inside the value. sortRecursive ksorts so insertion order can't change the canonical bytes.
Q: Could a queue retry of finalizePaidKioskOrder allocate a NEW fiscal_sequence_no on an already-sealed order? A: No. The guard is `if ($locked->fiscal_sequence_no === null)` so idempotent on replay.
Q: Could RetryFiscalAllocCommand reset fiscal_alloc_error_at on a row that already has a fiscal_sequence_no? A: No — the WHERE clause requires NULL sequence_no.

Q: Could a pilot-restrict bypass occur if AuditLogService::write itself throws (e.g. cache outage > 5s)? A: The audit write is inside try/catch (line 532-558) so on failure, Log::warning fires but the ValidationException still propagates — the user is still rejected, only the forensic record is degraded to warning level.

Q: Could an attacker exploit the manager-gate routine-close to lock out a single-cashier deploy? A: Only if they can flip CASH_MANAGER_GATE_ROUTINE_CLOSE=true — that requires .env write access, which means full system compromise anyway.
regressions_seen_during_recent_history: None. The P0-POS-02 gateway-context guard (commit ce23352ab — Wave 3) and the iter15-P0-10 split-payment refund mirror payments are recent hardening, both with comprehensive comments and tests.
verdict: GREEN. Security surface on POS x Fiscal is at production-grade NF525 maturity. 0 P0, 0 P1, 2 P2 informational nits (env-cache pitfall + dev_sentinels growth), 8 KEEP-AS-IS attestations.
